segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
They abstained from milk, cheese, fat, and eggs during it,
and observed it like the rest of the days of the Fast.
And in the sixth year of Marcian, Valentinian of Rome was killed.
And from here, just as the Church was split in two,
for it was the custom {or: law} that whenever the emperor of Constantinople passed away,
by the agreement of the one in Rome an emperor was established;
and likewise, whenever the one of Rome passed away,
by the agreement of the one in Constantinople an emperor was established for Rome.
And because Marcian had arisen without the agreement of Valentinian of Rome, through the choice of Pulcheria who was co-ruling with him,
so the Romans, without the agreement of Marcian, set up an emperor for themselves.
Therefore the chroniclers in the East took care only of the emperors of Constantinople,
and recorded them one after another,
and they called them the emperors of the Romans.
And because Marcian and Pulcheria reigned in their old age,
they died without offspring.
After him, Leo, eighteen years.
He was Thracian by race,
and a tribune by rank.
He was chosen by the Senate and became emperor.
And in that same year, Peroz reigned over the Persians after Bahram son of Yazdegerd;
and he waged war against the Romans and persecuted the Christians.
And Leo gave his daughter Ariadne to Zeno,
and magnified him in the kingdom,
and made him general of all the East;
and he made Basiliscus general of Thrace.
And he built Callinicus,
and it was called Leontopolis.
And at this time a great fire broke out in Constantinople,
when the fire dominated from sea to sea.
And the emperor fled to the other side of Saint Mamas,
and stayed there six months.
And he built the great harbour of Neorion Embolon {OCR?}, and enacted a law
that no one should work on Sunday,
nor make use of any musical instrument,
but that everyone should be occupied in the churches.
And this Leo proclaimed his grandson Leontius (that is, Leo II),
namely the son of Zeno,
as Caesar while he was still a child of six years;
and he reigned for one year during his lifetime.
